```python
def dedupe_by_id(items):
    """Remove duplicate dicts by their 'id' key.

    Keeps the last occurrence of each id, but each id stays at the
    position where it first appeared.
    """
    by_id = {}
    for item in items:
        by_id[item['id']] = item  # re-assigning an existing key updates the value but keeps its position
    return list(by_id.values())


if __name__ == '__main__':
    records = [
        {'id': 1, 'name': 'a'},
        {'id': 2, 'name': 'b'},
        {'id': 1, 'name': 'c'},
        {'id': 3, 'name': 'd'},
        {'id': 2, 'name': 'e'},
    ]
    print(dedupe_by_id(records))
    # [{'id': 1, 'name': 'c'}, {'id': 2, 'name': 'e'}, {'id': 3, 'name': 'd'}]
```

This relies on dicts preserving insertion order (guaranteed since Python 3.7). Reassigning an existing key replaces its value without moving it, so each id keeps its first-appearance position while holding its last-occurrence dict.
